transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced technical support, my name is Gareth. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Gareth, my name is Rhiannon Davies. Every single night around three in the morning when our S-Net Hub 5 performs its scheduled maintenance reboot, all custom port forwarding rules configured for our TrueNAS file server and security NVR disappear completely from the router's configuration table, severing remote access for our off-site backup servers!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Rhiannon. If I understand correctly, your S-Net Hub 5 is failing to retain custom port forwarding rules in non-volatile flash memory across scheduled overnight reboots, severing remote access to your TrueNAS server and security NVR. Before we inspect your router's NVRAM firmware registers, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 28 Cathedral Road, Cardiff, CF11 9LJ, security PIN 5541, customer account BB-881920.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Rhiannon, that confirms your account details. Have you configured static DHCP reservations for both the TrueNAS server and the security NVR on the local subnet?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, TrueNAS is statically mapped to 192.168.1.50 and the NVR is mapped to 192.168.1.60 with their MAC addresses bound in the router GUI.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your Hub 5 cloud configuration sync state and NVRAM commit logs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Rhiannon. The firmware telemetry confirms that while the web GUI accepts port forwarding rules, the local NVRAM commit daemon was encountering a write lock timeout against the TR-069 cloud provisioning profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why was the cloud provisioning profile creating a write lock timeout on local NVRAM?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When firmware version 4.12 was deployed, an unhandled concurrency bug caused the cloud TR-069 parameter sync to overwrite local firewall tables with the default empty profile upon reboot initialization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you patch the firmware or push an updated cloud profile that preserves local firewall rules?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, we have released firmware maintenance patch version 4.12.3 which specifically fixes the TR-069 firewall table persistence synchronization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we flash firmware patch 4.12.3 to our Hub 5 right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am pushing the firmware patch 4.12.3 image directly to your Hub 5 flash memory.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub center light turned solid orange... now it is flashing cyan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The flash memory write takes approximately ninety seconds to complete.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The light has returned to solid green. Has the firmware update succeeded?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Firmware version 4.12.3 is now active with commit validation verified.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now can we configure the port forwarding rules directly into the cloud profile?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously port forwarding tables require clean TCP and UDP port mappings bound to verified local IP endpoints.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I have the exact port numbers ready: port 22 and 443 for TrueNAS, and port 8000 and 8554 for the NVR.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Rhiannon speaking, our medical practice off-site backup server synchronizes confidential patient dental records across that TrueNAS tunnel between midnight and five in the morning! Because your router wiped the port forwarding rules every night this week, four consecutive off-site backups failed and our practice faced an immediate regulatory audit breach under healthcare compliance rules! I have been sick with worry, working until 4 AM trying to re-enter rules manually! We cannot afford another failed backup tonight!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the immense pressure, regulatory anxiety, and exhausting late nights this has caused you and your dental practice, Rhiannon. Missing patient record compliance backups is an absolute critical emergency, and I will ensure these port forwarding rules are permanently committed and personally verify their persistence through a live test reboot right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Gareth, that is exactly what I need to have total confidence.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am binding port 22 and 443 to 192.168.1.50 for TrueNAS, and port 8000 and 8554 to 192.168.1.60 for the NVR directly on your primary cloud profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The rules just populated in the hub web GUI!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now I am triggering an explicit hardware write commit to sync the cloud profile to local non-volatile flash memory.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Flash commit confirmed: 'NVRAM sync status: SUCCESS'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us initiate a deliberate remote restart of the Hub 5 to simulate the overnight maintenance reboot while we are on the call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Rebooting the hub now... The connection dropped... Hub is restarting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router will complete its boot initialization and reload its NVRAM tables in approximately two minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub light is flashing green... and now it turned solid green again! Internet is restored!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please open the hub administration dashboard and check the Port Forwarding tab.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Logging into 192.168.1.1... Navigating to Port Forwarding... Gareth! All four rules are still there! TrueNAS ports 22 and 443, and NVR ports 8000 and 8554 are intact!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent! Now let us test external connectivity to verify the TrueNAS port from outside your local network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am using my mobile phone with Wi-Fi turned off to query port 443 on our public IP... Gareth! The TrueNAS SSL login page loaded immediately over cellular!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms full bidirectional port forwarding persistence across physical router reboots.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tonight's patient dental record backup will execute with zero errors.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked the cloud profile preventing any future firmware updates from overriding user-defined firewall tables.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have completely saved our practice from regulatory audit sanctions, Gareth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented all firmware revisions and port rules under case reference ADV-PORT-99182-R.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: ADV-PORT-99182-R, recorded in our IT maintenance log.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated configuration backup system will also archive your port rules every twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That provides total redundancy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just making sure I have the exact account reference for our engineering log: that was BB-881920, wasn't it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, BB-881920 is our business account reference.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Rhiannon, all configuration records and audit logs are fully committed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for your world-class expertise and rapid resolution today, Gareth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure assisting you, Rhiannon. Best of luck with your dental practice backups.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Have a wonderful rest of your day, Gareth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other advanced technical query I can assist you with today, Rhiannon?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Gareth, you have fixed everything perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced technical support, Rhiannon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Gareth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
